target_customer: Institutional investors buying consumer loans, and lenders originating them
problem: Consumer credit was underwritten inefficiently; Theorem used machine learning to underwrite loans bought for institutional capital and securitized.
business_model: Asset manager fees on consumer credit funds and securitization services
product_category: Consumer credit asset management and ML underwriting

founders.name: Abeer Agrawal
education: Carnegie Mellon University, electrical and computer engineering and computational finance (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Later moved to Levro per YC page.

founders.name: Hugh Edmundson
prior_employers: Morgan Stanley (credit derivatives team, per a jobs listing)
founders.background_notes: Later called Chairman and CIO in a press release.

competitors.name: Lending Club and Prosper
competitors.what: Online marketplace lenders selling loans to investors
competitors.traction_then: About 98 percent of the US marketplace lending market in 2014; Lending Club disbursed over 4 billion and Prosper 1.6 billion

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a machine learning underwriting model and securitization pipeline for consumer credit required quantitative finance, data and capital structuring.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary loan performance data and institutional capital relationships compound, but other lenders and funds can build models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pagaya agreed to acquire Theorem in July 2024, expecting to close in Q4 2024.

market_need_then: Marketplace lending was growing quickly in 2014 and institutional buyers were taking the loans, but Theorem did not appear in any 2014 sources found.

branding.domain_note: Uses theoremlp.com, a suffixed domain, suggesting theorem.com was unavailable; not stated by a source.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'Hello World, We're Theorem' on current site

brand_strength.rationale: Institutional finance brand with press releases about ABS deals, but no community or brand coverage. Confusable with other Theorem companies in search.

outcome_analysis: Theorem grew from a 2014 YC startup into an institutional manager of consumer credit funds, described as managing over 2.2 billion in net assets and having bought over 9 billion of loans per a search summary of its materials. Pagaya agreed to buy it in July 2024 for an undisclosed sum, a successful outcome though value is unknown.
notes: No reliable funding found. Crunchbase lists Series Unknown and Simplify says 2.6M seed; unverified and one page contains unreliable mock data. Pagaya press release (BusinessWire) returned 403; deal facts come from a search summary of FinTech Futures and Bloomberg coverage. The competitor entry is from a 2015 paper describing the 2014 market, not Theorem specific. The AUM figures come from a search summary, not opened.
